skills.summary: Sort an inbox dump into act, reply, defer
skills.job: Sort a pasted batch of emails into do now, reply, delegate, defer and ignore, with a one-line next action each.
gotchas: Ranking by sender instead of deadline
Missing a buried question in a long thread
Marking a waiting-on-me item as informational

skills.summary: Nudge someone who has not replied
skills.job: Write a follow-up to an unanswered message that restates the ask and makes replying easy without nagging.
gotchas: Apologising for bothering them
Repeating the whole first email
Changing the ask between follow-ups

skills.summary: First email to a stranger that gets read
skills.job: Draft a short first-contact email to someone who does not know the sender, with one specific reason and one small ask.
triggers: reach out to someone I do not know
gotchas: Opening with the sender's biography
Mass-mail phrasing with an unfilled merge field
Asking for a call before giving any reason

skills.job: Write a work apology that names what went wrong, owns it, states the fix and does not grovel.
triggers: I messed up, write an apology
gotchas: Passive voice that hides who erred
Explaining so long it reads as an excuse
Promising a fix date the user cannot meet

skills.summary: Ask for a meeting with a clear purpose
skills.job: Write a meeting request with purpose, length, proposed times and what the guest needs to prepare.
gotchas: Offering no times so the thread drags on
Ignoring time zones
Asking for an hour when fifteen minutes would do

skills.summary: Say no without burning the bridge
skills.job: Write a clear refusal to an invitation, request or offer that is kind, short and leaves no false opening.
gotchas: Writing maybe when the answer is no
Inventing a fake excuse that can be checked
Burying the no in the third paragraph

skills.summary: Progress report a busy reader can scan
skills.job: Turn rough notes into a status update with done, next, blocked and asks, led by the one thing the reader must know.
gotchas: Listing activity instead of outcomes
Hiding a slipped date at the bottom
Using green status when a risk is open

skills.summary: Prepare for a hard talk at work
skills.job: Prepare the user for a tense workplace conversation: goal, opening line, key points, likely replies and a fallback.
triggers: I have to tell my boss something hard
prepare me for a tough conversation
how do I give this feedback
gotchas: Scripting the whole talk instead of the opening
Leading with the cushion so the point is lost
Skipping the question of what outcome is acceptable

skills.summary: Short chat messages that get answers
skills.job: Write or tighten a Slack or Teams message so it can be understood and acted on without a follow-up question.
triggers: how should I word this in chat
gotchas: Sending a bare hi and waiting for a reply
Burying the ask under context
Tagging a whole channel for a one-person question

skills.summary: Thank-you note with a real detail
skills.job: Write a thank-you after an interview, gift, favour or help that names a specific thing the person did.
gotchas: Generic gratitude with no detail
Adding a new ask inside the thanks
Waiting a week after an interview

skills.summary: Counter an offer or price by email
skills.job: Draft a negotiation email that states a position, gives the reason and leaves room to agree, for salary, rates or vendors.
gotchas: Naming a number without a basis
Giving a range whose bottom is the real target
Threatening to walk away without meaning it

skills.summary: Escalate a stuck issue to a manager
skills.job: Write a message that raises a blocked issue to someone with authority, with history, impact and the decision needed.
triggers: they are not responding, go higher
gotchas: Blaming a person instead of describing the blockage
Leaving out what was already tried
Not saying what decision or action is wanted

skills.summary: Consumer complaint with a clear remedy
skills.job: Write a consumer complaint to a company about a product or service, with facts, dates and the remedy wanted. Not a legal document.
triggers: ask for a refund by email
gotchas: Venting without stating the remedy
Missing order number or date
Citing consumer law from memory

skills.summary: Introduce two people with consent and context
skills.job: Write a double introduction between two people that says why they should talk and makes the next step easy.
triggers: connect my friend with a recruiter
gotchas: Introducing without asking one side first
Giving each person a different story of why
Leaving both to guess who writes first
